summary: Preinstall fetches Bun runtime and executes obfuscated 727 KB payload smuggled into tarball
details: On npm install, the package's preinstall hook (`node setup.mjs`) downloads a platform-specific Bun runtime archive from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/, extracts and chmods the Bun binary, and invokes it against `math_init.js` — a 727 KB heavily obfuscated JavaScript blob shipped at the tarball root. `math_init.js` uses a rotating string-array loader (`WV8StW` shift-rotator over an `n7gIxM` constant table) and hex-mangled identifiers with no readable strings, the canonical obfuscator.io loader shape. `setup.mjs` itself is obfuscated with `_0xNNNNNN` identifiers and inline string-lookup tables, unlike any normal prebuild-install wrapper. `package.json` declares `"files": ["dist"]`, but `math_init.js` is not listed anywhere in the manifest and is smuggled alongside the legitimate `dist/` output. Using a freshly downloaded alternate runtime to execute an opaque obfuscated blob at install time on every consumer machine is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern; the executed payload's behavior cannot be observed from the source but runs with the installing user's privileges and bypasses Node-based tooling.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
